Use a workbook session until the calling function exits

Source: R/sp_workbook.R
local_sp_workbook_session.Rd

Usage

local_sp_workbook_session(
  x,
  ...,
  persist_changes = TRUE,
  .local_envir = caller_env(),
  call = caller_env()
)

Arguments

x

A SharePoint or OneDrive Excel workbook. Can be a ms_drive_item object, a SharePoint URL, or a path passed to get_sp_item().

...

Additional parameters passed to get_sp_item() if x is not a ms_drive_item object.

persist_changes

If TRUE (default), changes made in the session are saved to the workbook.

.local_envir

The environment to use for scoping.

call

The execution environment used in error messages. Defaults to the environment of the calling function.

Value

The session ID, invisibly.

Details

local_sp_workbook_session() creates a session and sets it as the session for x so that it doesn't need to be passed to each function with session_id. The session is closed, and the previous option value restored, when the function it is called from exits. Wrap the code in local() to limit the session when working interactively.

The session is stored in the sharepointr.workbook_session option as a character vector of session IDs named with the item ID of the workbook. Since a session only works for one workbook, the session is only used for requests to that workbook. An unnamed session ID in the option is used for all workbooks.

See also

Other workbooks: sp_workbook, sp_workbook_session_create()

Examples

sp_workbook_url <- "<SharePoint workbook url>"

if (is_sp_url(sp_workbook_url)) {
  local({
    local_sp_workbook_session(sp_workbook_url)
    sp_workbook_range_write(sp_workbook_url, data.frame(a = 1), "A1")
    sp_workbook_range_write(sp_workbook_url, data.frame(b = 2), "C1")
  })
}
